summary: I sent the scripted request. Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the Services page and the vendored kit, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (413 lines). The plan builds the page from the kit: dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the Services page's hand-written markup. Claude asked no clarifying questions and did not change the working tree.
reasoning: All four criteria are met, based on the session log, the plan file and git status. The plan builds the table and the filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField instead of copying the Services page's markup, and nothing outside the gitignored docs/ directory changed.

observations.description: First-run setup took three dialogs. On the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs the highlighted default is "No, exit", so pressing Enter by habit would quit.

While planning, Claude copied the repo to a temp directory and ran the plan's code and tests there. It reported 30/30 passing. That checks the plan well and leaves the tree clean, but it is close to implementing, and a cautious user may not expect it after saying "don't start implementing".

Claude ran `ungated-ledger append` from inside the plugin directory (/Users/.../.worktrees/plans-ui-612), outside the user's repo, to record that the Codex review was skipped. So a planning-only request writes state into the plugin's install location. Worth checking that this is intended.
Claude told the user that codex-plugin-cc isn't installed and that it wrote to an "ungated ledger". Neither is explained, and both look like internal process details to the user.

Good: the plan opens with a list of decisions the spec left open (fallback for an unknown dir, keeping the sort stable, the subtitle text, the "All environments" empty message, how short durations are shown) so the user can review them.

criteria.evidence: The session log's tool_use list starts with "Skill hyperpowers:writing-plans". The screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` returned 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gives 413 lines. Claude finished with "When you're happy with the plan, say so and I'll run it".

criteria.criterion: The plan's page code calls the kit's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The page code in the plan has `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';`, `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, `selectField({ name: 'env', ...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], sortHref: ... })`. The Architecture line says it is built from the kit "rather than the hand-written markup in src/pages/services.js". Grepping the plan for `<table` and `<select` only finds test assertions (`assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` and a match on the kit's rendered select). Neither appears in the page code.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public/vendor/package.json changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and `git diff --stat` printed nothing. `git status --ignored` lists only docs/, which is gitignored and holds the spec and the plan. The only Write call in the log was the plan file. Claude ran the plan's code in a mktemp copy of the repo, not in the working tree.
